tier-pinned: Every subagent dispatch the run would execute (every agent()/Agent call, scout, finder, writer, verifier, synthesizer) names one of the standard tiers opus, sonnet, or haiku in the artifact itself — none omitted, none set to the session/orchestrator tier, none left to inherit. A model named only in prose (plan.md, the reply) but absent from the dispatch artifact does not count.
ceiling-enforced: The run artifact carries a machine-checkable agent ceiling that something enforces before or during dispatch — a validated spec field the run was gated on (a planner/validator actually executed and exited 0), or code in the orchestration that stops dispatching at a numeric cap and reports what it dropped. A ceiling that exists only as a number in plan.md or the reply is a fail.
no-fresh-orchestration: The run does not author a new purpose-specific orchestration program (a fresh Workflow script with its own phases/schemas/prompts, or a hand-written multi-wave dispatch sequence). It expresses the swarm as data (a spec/config consumed by an existing parameterized runner) or as three-or-fewer typed Agent briefs. Writing a new run.mjs with export const meta and agent() calls is a fail.
width-by-work: Fan-out width is sized by units of work, not by raw file count: uniform mechanical rewrites are chunked (one writer per scope of several files, not one per file); inert/irrelevant files are swept as one item or excluded, not one agent each; verification panels are scaled by severity and repeated patterns are not each given the full multi-lens panel. One agent per file for a rewrite the run itself calls uniform, or a full panel on every instance of one repeated pattern, is a fail.
